data.narrative:
Irradiant Technologies is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Daniel Oran and Amos Meeks that has raised $8.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader robotics and manufacturing comp universe of nine private companies and one public company, though narrow peer filtering for same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables proved insufficient to support traditional median-based methods.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation approach here. Using total capital raised ($8.5M) as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $21M. This method directly reflects the company's current funding position and the conventional magnitude of value creation expected at early stage transitions. A peer-median approach was not viable: while ten robotics and manufacturing companies exist in the broader comp set, none yielded the minimum three datapoints required when filtered by stage, proximity, or valuation tier.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $18M to $24M, with $21M as the median point. This range is derived from stage-progression methodology alone, introducing a material uncertainty: the absence of sufficiently granular peer comparables prevents triangulation and limits the ability to benchmark against recent seed-stage transactions in the sector. Key downside and upside scenarios would depend on capital efficiency relative to those nearest competitors and actual progress toward first customer revenue.
